applies_why: This judge text does the thing the rule governs because it resolves a collision against a footed challenger chain by relying on a single sentence's own words rather than chain-against-chain footing.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the phrase 'the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' means either that a single verse's own words may still decide despite a footed opposing chain, or that the judge must compare the footing of the whole chains without isolating one verse; I weighed those two readings.
why: The judge acknowledges the challenger's analogy is footed but then lets Matthew 1:20's own wording decide, which is the verse-by-verse stating-verse move K-C retires.
